title: Super Mario Party
subtitle: Separate paths return to the party
summary: Super Mario Party is NDcube's first Switch entry, released on 5 October 2018.
body: Super Mario Party is NDcube's first Switch entry, released on 5 October 2018. Players again travel independently around boards, collecting coins and purchasing Stars while minigames interrupt each round. A single Joy-Con provides each person's controls, allowing motion sensing and HD Rumble to shape the short activities. The return to separate routes restores a familiar kind of rivalry: the next turn concerns the player's own position, the nearest prize and what the other characters might do before that destination can be reached.

Each character brings an alternative dice block with a particular set of outcomes. Choosing between it and the standard die makes movement partly a question of risk, with some characters favoring reliable numbers and others offering a larger reward alongside a possible loss. Recruited allies contribute additional rolls and lend their own dice. A useful partnership therefore changes the options available on a later turn, giving character selection and recruitment a practical role in planning a route around the board.

Eighty minigames provide different mixtures of individual competition, teams and motion control. Other modes place cooperation more centrally, extending the gathering beyond a single race for Stars. The score was composed by Masayoshi Ishi, Toshiki Aida, Satoshi Okubo and Naruki Kadosaka. Super Mario Party combines a return to the older board structure with ideas drawn from Switch's small, shareable controllers. Its changes are most visible in the hands of the group: each participant has a personal dice choice, but another ally or a cooperative challenge can change the relationship for a moment.
